entries.text: `junkfather own` starts a command in a process group of its own and records its owner (Claude Code session, subagent, lane; Codex thread; or the calling process), TTL, pgid, command and cwd. Attached it passes output and exit status through and stops the group on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP; `--detach` runs it under a supervisor with output to a log and returns at once. The TTL is enforced on the spot.
`junkfather adopt PID` owns a process that already runs.

`junkfather reap` ends entries by id, owner, subagent, lane or pid: SIGTERM, a grace period, SIGKILL, only to processes whose start time and command were verified, so a reused pid is never signalled. `--keep-for session` entries survive their subagent's stop; `junkfather hand ID --to SESSION` gives an entry to another session; `junkfather extend ID --ttl D` renews its TTL.
`junkfather hook` for Claude Code's `SubagentStop`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop` and `PreToolUse` (which subagent ran a command), registered through Mastack's lifecycle hooks by `install.py --mastack`.

`junkfather sweep` reaps expired entries and entries whose owner session is gone (Claude Code's session registry, the recorded process), and reports, without stopping them, unowned processes in agent scratchpads and worktrees; `reap --pid PID --force` stops one it listed. `sweep --plist` and `install.py --launchd` run it hourly.
`junkfather list [--json]` shows what runs, whose it is, its age and its TTL left.

`events.jsonl` records every start, adoption, exit, extension, hand-over, reap and sweep in Godfather's event schema version 1; `junkfather status --json` and `junkfather capabilities --json` give Godfather's dashboard its snapshot and contract.
